content:
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for service=ai-prefetcher image=prefetch-v3 region=us-west-2 canary=10%

sam: seeing a spike in 5xx from the inference proxy, looks correlated with the canary start ~ T+2m

maya: alerted on increased 502/504s from ai-proxy; errors go from ~0.3% -> 7% in 3m. P95 latency jump too.

incident-bot: Paging oncall (pager duty) -> ry an: PRIMARY_ONCALL #eng-oncall @ryan

ryan: On call, looking at dashboards now. sending query to isolate canary traffic.

sam: logs show OOMs on prefetch-worker pods and subsequent 502s from the proxy: `OOMKilled` and `kubelet eviction` around T+3m.

maya: Noted. Canary pods are 2 of 20, but traffic routing seems sending more than expected to canary (maybe a routing rule mismatch).

ryan: Rolling back canary routing to 0% traffic now. running: `kubectl apply -f canary-traffic-cutoff.yaml`

deploy-bot: Canary traffic update: prefetched-model-v3 -> 0% in us-west-2 (config change applied) :white_check_mark:

sam: traffic to canary now ~0, but we still see errors from some frontends due to degraded cached connections and backend retries. Will drain canary pods.

ryan: Initiating drain: `kubectl cordon/evict` on canary nodes + `kubectl delete pods -l release=prefetch-v3 --grace-period=30`

support-bot: Customer impact alert: Affected requests ~12% of total AI requests in us-west-2 between 12:34-12:41 UTC, error rate peaked 18% for that window. No orders or billing impacts reported.

lia: opening a quick customer-facing blurb draft for CS: "We experienced elevated errors affecting model prefetching in us-west-2 during a canary rollout; mitigation in progress, no data loss". Will post once confirmed.

maya: Can we confirm feature-flag kill switch for prefetch is available? If routing rollback isn't enough, flip the ff.

ryan: Yes, `ff-admin toggle prefetch_models` exists. I prefer kill-switch now as a safe fallback. Executing: `ff-admin set prefetch_models false --env=us-west-2`

deploy-bot: Feature flag update: prefetch_models=false applied to env=us-west-2 (actor=ryan) :lock:

sam: After FF toggle, error rate dropped to ~0.8% in 2 mins. P95 back to baseline. Looks effective.

support-bot: Updated CS blurb: "Issue mitigated; we disabled an experimental prefetch feature in us-west-2 which resolved the elevated errors. We're monitoring."

maya: Creating a short incident in incidents channel and assigning initial severity SEV2 (customer facing but limited scope).

ryan: Handoff: I need to hop off in 20m. Maya, can you take primary until finish? I'll document steps I've run.

maya: Taking over. Ryan - please drop the rollback commands you used and any relevant logs in the thread.

ryan: Pasted commands run:
```
# cut traffic
kubectl apply -f canary-traffic-cutoff.yaml
# drain pods
kubectl delete pod -l release=prefetch-v3 --grace-period=30
# feature flag
ff-admin set prefetch_models false --env=us-west-2
```
Relevant pod logs saved to s3://redwood-logs/1965432100/pods.tar.gz (ryan)

sam: Noted. I'll start a short smoke run across common prompts and watch for regressions.

lia: CS updated customers in impacted cohort (alpha partners) with the blurb. No customer escalations yet.

maya: Monitoring looks stable for 10 minutes. We're going to keep the FF off and hoist a config fix for resource limits on prefetch-worker before attempting any re-release.

support-bot: Incident record created: incident-1965432100, severity=SEV2, owner=eng-runtime, impact=partial service degradation in us-west-2, start_ts=1965432100

ryan: Logged a short timeline and actions in the incident doc. Handing primary to maya. I'll remain reachable for questions.

maya: Thanks. I'm keeping this as active for another hour for verification and will post next update in 30m.

sam: Follow-up note: root cause looks like an unexpected memory regression in prefetch-v3 image + traffic routing bug that amplified exposure. We'll need a rollout checklist update.

support-bot: Next update scheduled in 30 minutes. :calendar:
